Today appeared before the undersigned Excellencies, commissioned members from the Venerable Land Council here, Don Simon de sielve wijesiri Abenaijke arraatje under the Mohandiram and head of the kandebaddepattoe [a local administrative division], Don Constantino wissesoendre Abenaijke, being the declarant's brother, now detained, Christian, aged 35 years. Who, by order of the Excellent and commanding Lord Dessave [Governor] Willem Adriaan Berghuijs and by translation of the Land's sworn Interpreter Louis Ferdinandus, on the 15th of June 1791, declared as follows. That yesterday afternoon around half past one o'clock, while he was on his rice field, the aforementioned Mohandiram had summoned him, the declarant, and ordered him to bring a sealed ola [palm leaf letter], which had been brought to the guard post of Hakman and addressed in the name of the modliaar [local official] Jlangakoon, but which was wrapped in a piece of linen cloth, together with a laskorijn [messenger] to Mature [Matara] and to deliver the same to the aforementioned Modliaar, but if the modliaar should say so, to hand over that ola to the Excellent Lord Dessave, which he could do. That thereupon

It was yesterday evening already late when I had the honor to receive your Well-Born Esteemed, honored Missive of the 8th of this month. Thus I shall halt here tomorrow, and am the cini de Capelli of Angelbeek. 4794. ntous ibertus van Zitter. inlant. Absent. Copy. Apart secret. Colombo. To the Well-Born, Great Esteemed, Sir Wo: Willem Jacob van de Graaff, Ordinary Councilor of the Netherlands Indies, Governor and Director of the Island Ceylon with its subordinate territories, Together with l von Drieberg, the Councilor. mnas Fretz: Hoest. anus Vallenhove. tavaka, the second at Maturziek. Well-Born, Strict, Great Esteemed, High Commanding Sir. By a letter of yesterday, the E. of the 15th of this month, the acting overste von Drieberg informed me that His Excellency, taking on the dessavoop march to Cattoen with a strength of 358 men, would accept the provisions from the dewalebadde. Although His Excellency showed that the notorious Don gebrek at koelies and otherwise the pattoe, accompanied by not all necessary provisions, was unable to take along; which the acting Mahampattse dessave DE Berghuijs should, as soon as possible, send. The aforementioned Excellency von Drieberg brings in his letter, of which the copy is enclosed herewith, several difficulties. Firstly, His Excellency finds that too small a garrison remains at Mature and more men must be sent there. Secondly, His Excellency supposes the possibility that in case of breach of peace with Kandy, our inhabitants might possibly become disloyal to us, and it would then be better to take a post between Mature and Fangale to cover both places than to march toward the king's land. And thirdly, His Excellency complains about the heads that, notwithstanding all the promises, they accomplish nothing, that the orders of the E. Berghuijs do not seem to be followed very well.

text_translated_detailed: His Excellency finds that too small a garrison remains at Mature and more men must be sent there. And thirdly, His Excellency complains about the heads that, notwithstanding all the promises, they accomplish nothing, that the orders of the E. Berghuijs do not seem to be followed very well, and that the Modliaer, who had promised to provide coolies and beasts of burden, to have the rice pounded and to send it to Cattoen, yesterday had not even departed from Mature to his district. Since everything that I have to remark concerning the aforementioned matter comes down again to what I have said so many times, namely that we can place little reliance on the willingness of our heads, as they would show this in this circumstance, the more so since it is sufficiently certain that they can provide in abundance whatever the land yields, be it rice, or coolies, draught oxen and so forth for a detachment, as the E. overste von Drieberg made clear, that the notorious Don pattoe, accompanied by his Mahampatta, if they are only willing; at the very least they should show themselves active. Furthermore, that we cannot abandon ourselves to the loyalty of our inhabitants, upon which these heads certainly have every possible power, I repeat that everything I have to remark concerning the condition of affairs in the Maturese dessavony would only be a repetition of what has already been said many times, so I shall not trouble your Well-Born Esteemed Great Excellency with this and only request that you cast a favorable reflection upon the contents of the E. overste von Drieberg's letter. I would gladly send more troops to Mature, but my own lack of resources places me in a position of inability, the more so since in case of disturbances, I must keep the road to Mature open and for that purpose I intend to take a post at Goijapane and Polwatte, which must be done from here. I request your Well-Born Esteemed Great Excellency, if it is possible, to send yet one Company of Malays or Europeans to Well-Born, Esteemed, Commanding Sir, Cited as Named in 1791. Present. I shall therefore hold here tomorrow, and am the Capelli 4736 of van Angelbeek. I am also sufficiently compelled to do so; since we from Angelbeek. today from fangale [uncertain: place name] up to here have experienced the heavy rain that fell yesterday and today, and have had a very difficult passage; The water between here and kattoene [uncertain: place name] is so high that it reaches up to the chest, thus I have a good pretext to rest here for some days and to await further orders. The road in the meantime was somewhat better, so I was, since I was already underway, also inclined to march these two hours further, which I shall do the day after tomorrow in hope of good tidings; for it seems to me that it is now better. From the 15th of this month received a letter from the merchant Berghuis, acting as the dessavonij [dessava: local administrator] of Mature, and a declaration from the vidaan [vidaan: local official] of the dewalebadde Don Philip named, whereby it became clear in detail that the notorious Don the pattoe [pattoe: local official], accompanied by his brother Don Simon Modliaar of the Mahampatta F Beukman is completely ready to go to kattoene, or to remain lying here—perhaps through haste it will come to a conclusion. I hear today that I perhaps without resistance can come to Collone korle [uncertain: place name] if I receive orders to march inland. Of both the Don Simons no one has appeared; the second Mondliaar [mondliaar: local official] of the Gerwaij tells me that they are very much on the Candianese side and themselves. text_translated_detailed: Decree Resolution Taken in Council of Ceylon Friday the 17th of June 1791. Present The Honorable and Most Esteemed Governor of Malabar, President Johan Gerard van Angelbeek, The Esteemed Chief Administrator Mattheus Petrus Raket, Colonel and Head of Artillery Elias Paravicini de capelli, Maturese Dessave [regional administrator] Mr. Christiaan van Angelbeek, First Warehouse Master Johannes Reintous, Secretary Benedictus Lambertus van Zitter, Commerce Bookkeeper Abraham Samlant. Absent The Honorable and Most Esteemed Governor Willem Jacob van de Graaf, The Esteemed Lieutenant Colonel and interim Chief of the Militia Diederich Carl von Drieberg, Dessave Diederich Thomas Fretz, Payroll Bookkeeper Gerrit Engel Holst, Fiscal Johannes Adrianus Wallenhove the first and third at Sitavaka, the second at Mature and the last two sick. There was read a letter from Gale under covering letters of the 15th of this month from the merchant Berghuis, acting as dessave of Mature, and a declaration from the vidaan [local official] of the Dewalebadde named Don Philip, by which it became clearly evident that the notorious Don Simon Mohandiram of the Gangebadde pattoe [district], accompanied by his brother Don Simon Modliaar of the Mahampatta on the 17th of June 1791, was indeed engaged in attempting to incite the inhabitants of his district, as well as those of the Morrua and Belligam korl [divisions], anew to rebellion and defection: therefore it was deemed good and understood beforehand that the declaration should be inserted here. Report given by lankamoelle [local official]

De Mohandiram van de kandebad depattoe het wijders daar ter plaatse zelfs met birrees rondtrommelen, dat de Jngeseetenen tot eene tesaamen rottings bij hem moesten verscheinen; zendende tevens bodons naar de Morruakorle en de Billigam korle met aankondiging aan de gemeente aldaar dat de revolte heeden in zijne pattoe zoude uitbreeken en zij zich ook aldaar tot het munten moesten tesaamen spannen zeggende voorts aan mij dat zoo de revolte in zijne Pattoe een aanvang genoomen heeft, de kandiaanen met de Maturesche Jngeseetenen zouden konjungeeren. Tot gister nademiddag te vier uwen ben ik bij den Mohandiram gebleeven, zonder verlof te konnen krijgen om te vertrekken, tot dat hij het mij eindelijk permitteerde, zeggende dat ik het als een gunst moeste aanmerken, wijl hij als Arraatje mij van voor nu eenige tijd afkende maar dat ik in 't vervolg niet moeste onderstaa, om Den 17. Junij 1791: in zijn pattoe te koomen, tot het oproepen van volk, wijl hij het volstrekt aan allen verbieden

Speaking thus, we encountered two laskorins on the road, whom the Mohandiram asked where they were going, and when they replied that they were going to Mature to depart for the command, he prevented this and ordered them to return to their homes. These men, pleased about this, thanked the mohandiram for that favor, however he took them into his company and drew them among the aforementioned peoples gathered together for the mutiny. Continuing our way, we arrived at Deij andre, while the brother of the aforementioned Mohandiram, being the Head of the Magampattoe, arrived in the company of his wife being carried in a palenkein [palanquin] and accompanied by much people, and without saying anything went to the Rest house. The Mohandiram of the kandebaddepattoe furthermore there at that place himself with birrees [armed men] drummed about, so that the inhabitants had to gather together at him; sending at the same time messengers to the Morruakorle and the Billigam korle with announcement to the community there that the revolt would break out today in his pattoe and they should also gather together there for the mutiny, saying further to me that if the revolt had begun in his Pattoe, the Kandyans would join with the Maturese inhabitants. Until yesterday afternoon at four o'clock I remained with the Mohandiram, without being able to obtain permission to depart, until he finally permitted it to me, saying that I should regard it as a favor, since he as Arraatje [headman] had known me for some time before, but that I should not dare in the future to come into his pattoe to call up men, since he would absolutely forbid it to everyone

text_translated_detailed: I have received certain news that the Dessaves [regional administrators] of the Seven Korles [Korles: a district/administrative division] broke camp on Sunday night from Kornagelle [Kornagelle: a place name], and proceeded to the village of New Pandanigid, which is two miles from Kornagelle, and are now stationed at the rest house of Kandoemoelle, which is three hours' journey from Kornagelle. They have with them three thousand Singalese with firearms, though among them there are neither Malabar soldiers nor Sipahis [Sipahis: mounted soldiers/cavalry]. At the aforementioned rest house they will remain for several days, and from there they will proceed to Keppetiewatane, Gallelle, and Macandoere. Macandoere is three and one-quarter miles from the village of Singacoelij in the Pittigalkonle, at which place in the previous war a heavy detachment was stationed. The King's brother, for whom a palace has been built at Kornagelle, is expected at all hours, together with the Dessave of Matele, and they will arrive with a heavy force, among which there are many Malabars and Sipahis. According to rumors here, they will have seven elephants and various war munitions have been brought to Kornagelle, among which there are also said to be three cannons. The Dessave of the Seven Korles has had the Madoege or Moorish Dessave flogged with a cane for a transgression committed, and has subsequently dismissed him from his service, sending him to the Court of Kandy [Kandy: the capital of the Kandyan kingdom]. The Dessave of Matele is very discontented that the Dessavony [administrative position] of the Seven Korles was not granted to him, and because he lives in enmity with the present Dessave of the Seven Korles, for this reason he has kept himself away and has not come to Kornagelle until now. But since he has now moved away from Kornagelle, he is expected at all moments there together with the King's brother. However, where they will go after that is as yet unknown. Nevertheless, it seems now that matters will come to actual hostilities. I fear for Silau [Silau: a place name]. Just now I receive

Colombo. To the well-born Sir D.D. van Ranhow, merchant and chief of Negombo and Silau. In the enclosed letter I present to your well-born, on the urgent matter, a translation of which original I have just received from the Modliaar [uncertain: local administrator] of Madampe. For the protection of our land there is not the slightest watch post, so that they can come by night to take away the possessions of our inhabitants and cause them all harm. Van onze singaleesche Hoofden word niets gevraagt, maar de Naijkers die thans present zijn en zig voor konings van „den opgeeven. De Mooren Naijkers en den koning, na hun believen eenige lande „rije van de Jngesetenen ontnomen hebben. „de zeggen dat zij de Distrikten moeten afneemen en met voorneemen om na den overwal te gaan hebben nu voor drie maanden onder voorgaave van Misdadigen te zijn daar heen uijt het Hof laeten vertrekken; Buijten, des word uijt Dispens de Maintementos verstacht voor 14800. lascorijns en hoort men dat de uijt landers zijn op Baticaloa aan land gekoomen. De Singaliesen zijn van den beginne af, niet ontrouw geweest wier volgen eenige woorden die onduijdelijk zijn en scijnen te zeggen dat de koning geen ver- „trouwen in de Singaleesen stelt en dat tot ongeluk zal strekken, ingevalle deese dingen rugbaar wierd / Naar uwes goeddunken konnen wij de weegen aantoonen en dan oorlog staat te ge- schieden egter moeten uwes daar voor niet vreezen en zullen wij de mogelijke hulpe bewijzen. Twee mohandikams gem: opperhoofd was gezonden. Aldus door vertolking van den pataniet tolk Moettoe wingoe desoren, also de relatant niet anders dan pattanies versting, en ook niet schrijven nog leesen kan, is dese in 't mallabaarsche overgeset en door mij ten papier gobragt te Jaffanapahiram den 31: Maart 1790. /was getekent/ Paul Franken Nagezien Beukman - aenoe moor naike „ 80. text_translated_detailed: Translation of Singhalese letter ola brought to the Honourable Dessave Fretz by the Kandyan. Nothing is asked of our Singhalese chiefs, but the Naykers [uncertain: possibly a local official or military rank] who are now present and present themselves as kings. The Moors, Naykers, and the king, according to their pleasure, have taken some lands free from the inhabitants. They say that they must take over the districts and with the intention to go to the other side, they have now for three months, under the pretext of being criminals, had them depart from the Court; Besides, from Dispens the Maintenances are expected for 14,800 lascorijns [uncertain: possibly a currency or measure], and one hears that foreigners have landed at Baticaloa. The Singhalese have not been disloyal from the beginning, whose following are some words that are unclear and seem to say that the king has no confidence in the Singhalese and that this will lead to misfortune, in case these things become known. According to your discretion we can show you the ways and then war is about to happen, yet you need not fear for that and we will provide whatever help is possible. Two mohandikams [uncertain: possibly a local official title] chief was sent. Thus through the interpretation of the Pattanies interpreter Moettoe wingoe desoren, since the informant understands nothing but Pattanies, and also cannot write or read, this has been translated into the Malabaric language and was put to paper by me at Jaffanapahiram on 31 March 1790. /was signed/ Paul Franken Examined Beukman - aenoe Moor naike. That the Court of Kandy is now in great turmoil, and the king has had all his chiefs summoned together and made a representation concerning their intention, and at the same time had told them that the Company was now very embittered toward them, and as he knew no way to satisfy the Company again, he therefore asked, yet received no answer from any of them regarding this, except only from the high priest, who had offered to seek a means to this end, which was granted to him by the king. Thereupon the same had said that he had a very good friend and acquaintance in the Company's land in the Napitig at Korle, being the coral of the Uduegaha-pattoe, to whom he would ask for advice, who could also at the same time speak with the European residing there, so that through this channel from the Well Noble Great Esteemed Lord Governor a favorable answer could be obtained, which the king had granted to that priest with the addition that if with the Company without great complications they could again become good friends, whereupon first through this way they wished to have a good assurance, then the Company would have free permission from the Court to peel cinnamon above the Berg Ballane, to which confirmation then at the first opportunity an embassy would come. Also beyond this, if thereby the Company would not be satisfied, they would also cede to your Nobility the place or river at Satergam where the stones are fished. Upon this I could give no answer nor was permitted to, except that the king's offer to the Company seemed reasonable enough, and that the high priest to the king

The second modliaa of the Porta, by order of the well-honored great and esteemed Mister Governor, having written to me, to gather information whether there are rest houses in the village of Neppettiwallaane in the 7th korls situated between Pilauw and wissenaire, made and the forests cleared, so I have for that purpose sent out spies, who upon their return said that there were no rest houses made nor forest cleared, nor people gathered together, but that orders had been given that when the Dessave of the 7th Korles should come to Kornagalle, then from each family 20 medits of rice, 20 cookers, 12 holders, 12 mats, together with salt, purriporoe and pepper sauce must be provided. The spies whom I sent to the 4th Kores have upon their return said that a Mohotiaar had come to Idelmapane, who is writing down the weapons of the favorable ones. That the porter people Anawolleas of the 4 Kores by Pasc's of the atte pattoe have been summoned, and last Thursday night departed to Kandia: /:understood:/ for the Translation /signed:/ J.G. The relators relate that they have heard that the Theuwer Sedoepadie was not at Ramanadewaram [Rameswaram:], but at Tiroepoeranie [Tirupati:], with 15,000 men, and that the said Sedoepadie, the priest of Rameswaram, together with the merchant at Kilkarre, Audekader Markaijr, and the second Poredanie [uncertain: possibly a local official title] of Ramanadewaram named Pramene Aijer, at Tirupati had summoned and taken into arrest. That the king of Kandia on a certain day summoned his following court nobles, namely Odogamp Adigaar, the dessave of Matule, Palagamp Adigaar, the dessave of the 7 korles, the dessave of Oewe named Gawada Neleme, the dessave of the three korles, and several other prominent court officials, to whom the king asked whether the peeling of cinnamon that is done by the servants of the Company in the king's territory could be permitted, in answer served by the assembled court nobles, excluding the dessave of Matule and the dessave of the seven korles, with a Yes, that the peeling of cinnamon by the Company in the king's territory could be granted, whereupon the dessave of Matule and that of the 7 korles.

From De Pettigodde I have heard that the Dessave of the seven korls at Nowekije Gahawatte is there with a great multitude of armed people, and the road to Gammedde has been cleared. An inhabitant from the village of Ponankanie in the Silause region, who came from Dekammadde, has reported to the undersigned. The Dessave of the seven korls is still at Dekammadde and has not come to Kawadiemoene. We have sent him two mortars, one arraatje [local official], and one kangaan [official], who have given orders to prepare a guard house there first, which has also been done, and the aforementioned four persons have returned first to Dekammadde. Antalang kawe is two and a half miles [modern equivalent: approximately 4 kilometers] from there. The aforementioned rest houses have been made, as the declarant himself has witnessed and seen. That within half a mile in a circle where the Dessave is located, everything is so occupied that there is no way through, and if it were discovered that it was an inhabitant of the Honorable Company, he would be killed without mercy. He further says that the aforementioned arraatje told him that over ten thousand Singhalese are with the aforementioned Dessave, and that half of them are not provided with firearms. From Kornegalle eleven elephants have come there, and when the goods from there have been taken, the elephants have been sent back to Kornegalle; a swarm of locusts has also been there. The Declarant testifies to have heard and seen the aforementioned.

Silauw, 19 June 1791. [was signed] I. W. Uhlenbeek. Agreed. Wijbrands.

At Ponnawebbe, half a mile [modern equivalent: approximately 0.8 kilometers] from Sarvette, a rest house for the Dessave of Matelle has been built today, and since this is certain, I give your Honorable Excellency notice of it, yet when he will come there is still unknown. Translation of a Singhalese letter ola [official letter/decree], dated 21 June 1791, written to the Honorable Governing Lord Dessave from Sitewake by the Mohandiram [official] of the Hewagamkorl.

The brother of the Dessave of Sappergam Ellepatte Ralehamij has been appointed as Pasnaike [official], and is ordered to occupy the battery with the people of the temple villages and the people of the Koerroewittikorl and Kendamgomme together with their chiefs. The former Pasnaike Eknelligodde Willame has been appointed as Attepa Hoeraale [official], and departed on the 19th of this month with the Dessave of Oewa of Battoegiddere toward Wallaalgodde, located in the Kollonakorl at the boundary.

text_translated_detailed: the Hewagamkorl [administrative district] Allahapenoeme. The brother of the Dessave [chief administrator] of Sappergam Ellepatte Ralehamij has been appointed as Pasnaike [military commander], and is ordered to garrison the battery at Gettehefte with the peoples of the temple villages, and the peoples of the Koerroewittikorl and Kendamgomme together with their chiefs. The former Pasnaike Eknelligodde Willame has been appointed as Attepa Hoeraale [title], and on the 19th of this month departed with the Dessave of Oewa of Battoegiddere toward Wallaalgodde, situated in the Kollonakorl at the boundary of Mature [Matara], and they are now at Denawakke. The aforementioned was reported to us today by a Poentje [local official] named Namamgamme and various other people. In the aforementioned battery at Gettehefte there are always over one hundred men, and it is said by some and others that these people were also supposed to come to Sitewake, yet no credence whatsoever should be given to this report. The Moors [Muslims] living hereabouts in the Company's territory have sent their women and children to Colombo. The Adigaar [high official] has issued an order to measure the arreek [tax/revenue] in the three korl [districts] and to work the moetettos [corvée labor]. A Vidaan [official] from the four korl, having come from the battery of Deijgille, has at the guard post of the king's [secret letter and will show] favorable 52 [uncertain: text appears damaged]. Extract from a letter of the bookkeeper Ripsema, dated the 22nd of this month, written from Silau to Nigombo. At Ponnawebbe, half a mile from Sarvette, a rest house for the Dessave of Matelle has been built today, and since this is certain, I give you, Your Honour, notice of it, but when he will come there is still unknown. Furthermore, I am now fully informed of the intentions of the Kandyans [people of Kandy], the Dessave of the 7 Corles will not come within our territory, before and unless he has won over our Pittigalkorlse [district] inhabitants [text becomes illegible/damaged]

Dated the 21st of June 1791. All those of the inhabitants of this korle who have come to know that the Great Adigaar of oedegompahase, together with the Dessaves of Saffergam and oeva, with their greater and lesser chiefs and such a great military force had departed, so that the places from omalpe and walalgodde to Battoegiddere, as it were, were filled, in order to fall upon these lands, are in such a death-like fear, nearly, that they, taking with them their wives, children, and goods, have retired into the forest and are setting up dwellings there for their safety. Through this uprising one can scarcely get to see any inhabitant, and I am likewise rendered completely unable to perform the Company's service. Thus I inform your Esteemed and Noble Lordship thereof most respectfully, and if your Esteemed and Noble Lordship would be pleased to grant me permission to come to Mature, it would be very agreeable to me. text_translated_detailed: Extract Missive dated 15th July 1791, written from Galle to Colombo: The acting dessave Berghius informed me that two participants in the leasehold salt pact, in the name Kokgelle Gangewage Simon and Ambe-nege Andries, reported that a great number of inhabitants, mostly consisting of Chindos and Wassers, accompanied by Namedde Gasweuwe Araetje and Pattetoepane Araetje, had given notice to their lessees that the Company, having abandoned the post Kirinde, this post had been taken into possession by the King of Kandy, and that they, the lessees, therefore had to depart from the leasehold. Against this they had objected that they could not do so without orders from their superior at Mature. Whereupon the aforementioned araetjes had advised their lessee with much urgency to depart from there at once, for if they did not do so, they would then be brought by the dessave of Saffergam. Whereupon the lessees found themselves obliged to depart. The Berghuis has had a record made of this report from the aforementioned lessees, of which a copy is enclosed herewith. The Berghuis supposes from the foregoing that it sufficiently appears that the minor headmen and the inhabitants of the Magampattoe, abandoning their lords and masters, have gone over to the King of Kandy, which evil, to prevent further [uncertain: original text], the Berghuis has requested the Colonel von Drieberg to send a detachment together with the newly appointed Mohandiram to the Magampattoe in order to apprehend and send away the rebellious araetjes and belhamers, since it does not yet appear that the Kandyans themselves have committed any acts on the Company's ground territory. [I believe still that:] as I have written to Colonel von Drieberg on the 8th, [one must try to appoint another head:] to the newly appointed mohandiram, whom one can trust has some influence over the minds of the inhabitants, to the Magampattoe, in order that through him, if possible, to bring the inhabitants back to their duty and to their obedience and loyalty to the Company, while I furthermore agree with Colonel von Drieberg that one should not divide the troops without necessity, since in case of war with Kandy it is very necessary to have the military force together, and furthermore, since, if peace remains and we are assured of this, our inhabitants will also easily be brought back to their duty.

I find myself now in the rest house Tawelowille on the Waluwe River, and since I now as a lowly person without the least help and assistance, am afraid to go among such ill-disposed people, I take the liberty of remaining here in expectation of a favorable and further order from your Noble Excellency. text_translated_detailed: Honorable Sir, Two inhabitants from the Silaude district have reported to the undersigned this morning that on the past Tuesday afternoon, the Dessave [expanded: chief administrator] of the 7th Corl [uncertain: administrative division] came from Kandia to Kornegalle, bringing with him 258 Kandyan Malays and approximately 30 or 40 Sipahees [expanded: Indian soldiers], and 500 Lascorijns [uncertain: type of soldier or laborer], all armed, and 12 pieces of sprinkkaanen [uncertain: type of cannon], as well as a quantity of ammunition, and for their provisions about 30 tamblies [uncertain: unit of measurement]. Shortly after the arrival of the aforementioned Dessave, he gave orders to immediately construct the road from Kornegalle to Badagalli Schoor, which was also immediately begun (the aforementioned place is 3½ miles from Kornegalle, in the direction of Tammerawille and Attenegalle). Iron cannonballs are being made from sprinkkaanen, and there are two warehouses with rice, and there are only some Lascorijns. Well, the Honorable Sir, in a secret letter and will make clear from favorable circumstances, having taken up residence in Kamansje, sent him out to ascertain where the Dessave is now staying. When the aforementioned Lewele Kamansje returned, he made it known that the Dessave is staying at Willitje alone, and that fully. The Kandyan Corijns [uncertain: type of official or soldier] who are stationed there, otherwise there is no people there. His residence is close to the secret letter of Your Excellency and will be clear from the favorable [text] in the file of Your Excellency, number 12. The boundary, I do not know what other reason this man could have had for this, except the fear of the recent revolt, of which he was a principal author, and he is the one who had the Bookkeeper thrown into prison. This man has in any case performed his service in the very best manner, and was also held in high regard by me. I sent him across to the other side with an ola [expanded: official letter] that he need fear nothing and should merely return, by which he became even more fearful. Also, the old kang [uncertain: possibly a title or position] who was arrested at the same time as the Coral, since the Coral said he had a chest in safekeeping with him, after I found him innocent, I released him again after having his house sealed, he went away absent. I imagine that this arrack merchant and kang must have conspired with the arrested Coral, since otherwise there would be no reason for the flight, of which however no evidence is known to me. I have placed an arrest on their buffalo and fields. I respectfully request Your Excellency's order. text_translated_detailed: Editor: Received: Mister Dessave. Half of the great road from Tamerawille onwards, all will come together at the village of Konouille and at Bakimarepe and at Kategambolle, where batteries will also be established. Ten days ago, at Dekkamande, seven elephants arrived with gunpowder and iron cannonballs; and after they were unloaded, they were sent back immediately to fetch more. text_original: De algemeene klagte of voorgevend muitelingen, blijkens de ontvangene relaasen, is dat maar eenige weinige van hunne gedaene klagten en verzoek zijn toegestaan geworden. volgens meer andere berichten is dit onder hun een algemeen zeggen. Tot deeze voorgaeve konnen, na het mij voorkomt, alleenig twee reedenen zijn. De eerste dat de mi „dere hoofden der zamenrotting om het gemeene volk aan hun snoer te houden, hun dit wijsmaeken, het welk het zelf is met te onderstellen dat de opstellen van de generaele klagt ola met voorda maar wijnige van de klagten der ingetenen hebben voortgebragt, om daar de gelijk in het eerste geval het volk in beroerte te houden, het tweede dat er waarlijk eenig bedrog met de generael klagt ola door eenige zeer weinige der hoofden der zamenrotting geschied is ond deeze twee is wel het eerste het waar schijnlijkste was het tweede geval wezend waar, dan zoude zeekerlijk de muitelingen wijl ze daar toe uitgenodigd zijn, met hunne waare klagte en verzoeken nader uitgekomen zijn zij hebben het teegendeel gedaen, en zelfs deeze uitnodiging met versmading van de hand geweesen. Het eerste geval diend dus wel als zeker aangenomen teworden, en men diend dit temeer te gelooven, wijl men voor het indienen der klagt olassen van verscheidene verzoeken die gedaan zouden worden, gehoord heeft, die men in de generaale klagt ola nog bij de partikuliere klagt olassen vind. onder deeze waaren een verzoek om de heffing van de nelie geregtigheid te veranderen, om de nieuwe gemaakte bepae „ling wegens de Jagerlatten en dorpsplanken, die te min geleeverd wierden weder op den vorigen voet te brengen, en om de brugge en basaar pagt afteschaffen. zoo het tweede geval met eenige waarschijnlijkheid kon aangenomen worden zo zoude daaromtrent een kort middel te vinden zijn, met afschriften van de generaele klagt
text_translated_detailed: The general complaint, or what the mutineers claim, according to the received reports, is that only very few of their made complaints and requests have been granted. According to several other accounts, this is a common saying among them. In my view, there can be only two reasons for this claim. The first is that the lesser leaders of the conspiracy, in order to keep the common people under their control, make them believe this, which itself is to be understood as the fact that the drafting of the general complaint has produced only few of the complaints of the inhabitants, in order thereby, as in the first case, to keep the people in unrest. The second is that there has truly been some deception with the general complaint by some very few of the leaders of the conspiracy. Of these two, the first is certainly the most probable. If the second case were true, then surely the mutineers, since they were invited to do so, would have come forward with their true complaints and requests. They have done the opposite, and have even rejected this invitation with disdain. The first case must therefore be accepted as certain, and one must believe this all the more because, before the submission of the complaint documents, one heard of various requests that would be made, which one does not find in the general complaint or in the particular complaint documents. Among these was a request to change the collection of the clove tax, to restore the newly made regulations concerning the hunter's allowances and village planks, which were delivered in insufficient quantity, to their former footing, and to abolish the bridge and bazaar tax. If the second case could be accepted with some probability, then a short remedy could be found in this matter, by sending copies of the general complaint

The first is that the lesser leaders of the conspiracy, in order to keep the common people under their control, make them believe this, which itself is to be understood as the fact that the drafting of the general complaint has produced only few of the complaints of the inhabitants, in order thereby, as in the first case, to keep the people in unrest. The second is that there has truly been some deception with the general complaint by some very few of the leaders of the conspiracy. Of these two, the first is certainly the most probable. If the second case were true, then surely the mutineers, since they were invited to do so, would have come forward with their true complaints and requests. They have done the opposite, and have even rejected this invitation with disdain. The first case must therefore be accepted as certain, and one must believe this all the more because, before the submission of the complaint documents, one heard of various requests that would be made, which one does not find in the general complaint or in the particular complaint documents. Among these was a request to change the collection of the clove tax, to restore the newly made regulations concerning the hunter's allowances and village planks, which were delivered in insufficient quantity, to their former footing, and to abolish the bridge and bazaar tax. If the second case could be accepted with some probability, then a short remedy could be found in this matter, by sending copies of the general complaint

Don Simon Aratje is a cunning fellow; he knows very well that a general pardon is the highest degree of goodness that a government can show to its subjects. Will he, being a traitor and having spurned this highest goodness, regard the further acts of kindness shown to him as anything other than snares laid for him, however holy the intentions of those bestowing this goodness may be? He will thus use this goodness to strengthen his influence over the sentiments of the mutineers, display his loyal adherence to their interests broadly, and thus gain ever more power to do harm. text_translated_detailed: Wijbrands, junior merchant and First sworn Clerk of Police here, the witnesses hereinafter named. Sinne Tambie segoe, a Moor and resident of Gale, who declared to speak the truth. That he once went to the Commandeur's sluice and requested a sannas for the felling of a mast timber for an inland vessel, which he obtained from His Honor and still has with him. That a day or three thereafter, or properly speaking on the 17th of April in the morning, he passed by the Commandement and the Commandeur Sluijsken called out to him and said that His Honor had received news that at Mature some mutineers had gathered together and some bridges had been broken down, and ordered him to go to Mature and to see what was the matter there. That he immediately thereafter departed for Mature and upon arriving at the river of Polwatte could not be transported across because the boats which were used for that purpose had been hauled onto the shore, and because he learned there that the mutineers had gathered at Dennepittie on the opposite side of the river of Kollenidande, he immediately turned back and arrived in the evening at Gale, and because the gate was already closed, he remained seen outside until the next day, when coming into the city he could not speak with the Commandeur because His Honor was in the meeting.
